title: Life-inspired interoceptive artificial intelligence for autonomous and adaptive agents - Nature Machine Intelligence
gist: A Perspective proposes 'interoceptive AI' -- giving artificial agents internal-state monitoring modeled on biological homeostasis -- as the missing ingredient for autonomous, continually adaptive agents, unifying free-energy-principle theory, reinforcement learning and neuromodulation research, and introduces the EVAAA benchmark to test it.

themes.theme: Interoception as a missing AI capability

insights.claim: Despite major advances in AI such as large language models, deep reinforcement learning and diffusion models, building agents that can autonomously pursue goals while continuously adapting to changing environments remains a fundamental unsolved problem, and biological interoception -- the internal monitoring and regulation of bodily states to maintain homeostasis -- is proposed as the missing ingredient.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Signals a research direction that could inform next-generation embodied/robotics agent architectures being built by robotics and agentic-AI labs, worth tracking as a precursor to product-level techniques.
insights.quote: Living organisms naturally exhibit such adaptive autonomy, offering a compelling source of inspiration for how artificial systems might achieve similar capabilities.

insights.claim: Internal states can function as a universally available and intrinsically valuable context that acts as a stable reference signal to modulate an agent's learning and behaviour even as the external environment changes, decoupling learned policies from ephemeral environmental circumstances.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Offers a design pattern for continual-learning agents that resist distribution shift and catastrophic forgetting, relevant to long-horizon autonomous robots and agentic systems operating in non-stationary environments.
insights.quote: internal states can also function as universally available and intrinsically valuable contexts, serving as stable reference signals that modulate learning and behaviour under changing external environments

insights.claim: Operationalizing interoception in an artificial system requires explicitly factorizing state variables into internal versus external environment components and mathematically formalizing 'life-inspired' properties (drawn from homeostasis and allostasis theory) that govern how internal states evolve over time.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Defines a concrete engineering checklist (state factorization plus dynamics formalization) that any team attempting to build interoceptive agents would need to implement, useful for evaluating competing research groups' claims in this space.

insights.claim: Incorporating neuromodulatory mechanisms -- biological signaling systems analogous to dopamine or serotonin modulation -- into agent architectures is proposed as a way to support context-dependent adaptive behaviour, implying neuromodulation-inspired network designs could improve an agent's ability to switch behavior modes as internal or external context shifts.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Points to a specific biologically-inspired mechanism (neuromodulation) that AI architecture researchers could borrow to build agents that handle regime changes better than static policies.
insights.quote: interoception-related biological processes, such as neuromodulatory mechanisms, can be incorporated to support context-dependent adaptive behaviour

insights.claim: The authors introduce EVAAA, a virtual-environment benchmark platform specifically built to test essential-variable-driven (interoceptive) autonomous and adaptive agents, indicating the field is moving from pure theory toward measurable, comparable benchmarks.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: A named, citable benchmark gives investors and technologists a concrete way to track whether interoceptive-AI methods actually outperform standard RL agents as follow-on papers use EVAAA to compare against this work.
insights.locator: Fig. 3: Overview of the EVAAA benchmark for implementing interoceptive AI

insights.claim: The paper is co-authored by Karl J. Friston, originator of the free-energy-principle/active-inference framework, alongside a South Korea-based Institute for Basic Science and Sungkyunkwan University group, with funding partly from South Korea's IITP 'Human Cognition-Based AI Core Technology' program.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: A credible link between an established theoretical framework (active inference) and applied agent design lends weight to this research direction, and flags South Korea's IITP as a funding source actively backing biologically-inspired AI programs worth tracking.

insights.claim: The authors explicitly frame interoceptive AI as a synthesis of cybernetics, theories of life, reinforcement learning and neuroscience, positioning it as a unifying theoretical account rather than a single narrow technique.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Signals this is intended as a foundational cross-disciplinary framework rather than an incremental method paper, meaning its influence (if adopted) would likely show up across multiple downstream subfields (robotics, RL, computational neuroscience) rather than one narrow niche.
insights.quote: this Perspective presents a unified account on how interoception can enhance autonomy and adaptivity in artificial agents by integrating insights from cybernetics with recent advances in theories of life, reinforcement learning and neuroscience
